$comment: Shared Go/TypeScript case table for the requirement status bridge's override-expiry window (shared/go/status.go and shared/typescript/status.ts). Every case is run by shared/go/status_test.go and shared/typescript/status.test.ts, so the two bridges cannot drift on what counts as an expiry. Each language decodes `requirement` with its own generated schema type, which is where the divergence lived: Go's StatusOverride.ExpiresAt is a non-pointer time.Time, so an absent expiry round-trips as the Go zero time 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z and decodes back to IsZero (never expires), while TypeScript carries the literal string and read it as an expiry in year 1.

cases.name: the Go zero time is no expiry
cases.note: What a Go-serialized override carries for an absent expiry; Go's IsZero check reads it back as never expiring, so the override still governs.

cases.name: the Go zero time with a millisecond fraction is no expiry
cases.note: A TypeScript consumer that re-serializes the quicktype Date emits the zero instant as 0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z; the fraction must not make it a real year-1 expiry.

cases.note: expiresAt is schema-required, but a malformed document can omit it; both bridges must read the absence the same way they read the Go zero time.
